systems.name: Relay v1 brain
systems.summary: Wanders, hunts, searches, chases, breaks doors; never leaves the map.

systems.name: Director (alarm panel)
systems.summary: Scoring core in main, not wired; Relay v2 step V0 (10-29 19:03, inert) brought it up to the 10-07 to 10-14 rules (phone walk, unlock, the rattle, the player-sees-it notice, no rehang) and added the floor-1 first-call hold and a full per-floor disarm. Since 10-30 11:35 (V3a) the director and the v2 loop are built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2, off until the bots pass and Red says yes (C02). Since 10-30 15:15 (V3c) a device tripped in a chase or a door break is heard and queued; it goes out at the next Away. Since 10-31 21:01 FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 is in the Standalone, WebGL and iPhone defines (交互设计, to switch body doors on, which are honoured only with it), so this loop is compiled into the 10-31 builds; C02 said v1 stays until the bots pass and Red says yes. Red decided it as C44 on 11-02: "用 v2，测试过了才用" (v2 ships only if the combined test's P0 chase and body-door rows pass). The playtest build 20261103-1434 (11-03 14:47, Mac and Windows) ships with v2 on; the combined test's P0 chase and body-door rows passed, G1 to G8 are not graded.

systems.name: Away, arrive, withdraw
systems.summary: It leaves, stays away, and returns at least 42 m from you. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 11:35 (V3a): arrive, step-in, the give-up beat, patrol from T3, withdraw and away; off until the flip (C02). Since 10-30 V3b adds its door licences (OPEN, BREAK only with a perception licence, WALL), Withdraw's one OPEN and the handoff, all behind the define. Since V4b it keeps one clock through its one look, so a look never buys time (G6).
systems.closed_note: Decided: v2 approved, after the Alpha (10-21)

systems.name: Noise meter
systems.summary: Sprints, barges and slams add up and call it; walking is almost free.

systems.name: Quiet-player sweep
systems.summary: After 240 s with no call it patrols the zone ahead of you. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 (V3b, the Q2 sweep); off until the flip (C02). Since 15:15 (V3c) waypoint 1 is picked where the Relay can step in and every leg keeps W ≥ 21 m, so a sweep no longer ends at its step-in.

systems.name: Tiers
systems.summary: Since 10-29 20:11 (Relay v2 step V1, on today's Relay): one tier per 150 new cells stood in (start rooms, stairwells, X and the station not counted), cap 5, never falls; the 120 s stall rise is gone (C04 a + b). Lamp odds are capped on every tier (stutter ≤ 20 %, failing ≤ 12 %). TIER is off the HUD and the CAUGHT screen (C04 c); only the optional RELAY READOUT assist shows it. The rest of v2's per-tier numbers are in main since 10-29 (V0, inert).

systems.name: Test bots
systems.summary: A tool: seeded bots measure the Relay before and after each step; its 15 measurement fixes are in main since 10-08, and its reports carry rule flags (E1, Floor 1 grace, A12, release cause) since 10-22. A follower mode walks the wall-cue arrows and checks they never point into glass or walls (10-22). The 10-22 smoke on v1 passed 8 of 8 (C05). No full matrix after the double-acting doors (Red 10-22: "不跑直接合"); the 10-08 Step 0 matrix stays the v1 reference. On 10-30 (harness r3.1, 14:44) it measured Floor 1's onboarding, B1's first encounter (2 seeds) and the first define-on smoke (1 seed, 8 runs, V3a + V3b only). The smoke grades no gate: RELAX gained 0 and G8 held on that seed; G5 waits for V4b. V4b's own 8-run smoke (seed 2554, 22:21): 6 chases, 2 lost, none by a bot trying to flee; the evader bots met no chase in 4 runs, so G5 is still unread, and their reaction clock has to start at the cue first.

systems.name: Path hearing
systems.summary: Sound follows real paths: a shut door or window adds 9 m; walls block.

systems.name: Sense links
systems.summary: A heard noise gives a rough estimate, never your exact spot. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 17:37 (V4a): the sense link, the estimate's error, repeats, margin decay and one re-target per 1.5 s; off until the flip (C02).

systems.name: Eyes and spotting
systems.summary: A 120° head cone to 12 m; a meter that fills faster up close. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); off until the flip (C02).

systems.name: Lock-on and chase
systems.summary: Warnings first, a 0.7 s hold and chime (1.7 s on an encounter's first lock-on within 9 m since V5, C37); chase capped at 4.4 m/s; the catch stays 0.7 m. Built behind FRONTROOMS_RELAY_V2 since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); off until the flip (C02).
systems.closed_note: Decided: keep 0.7 m, a longer hold on a close first sighting (10-30)

systems.name: Sight tests, prompt gate
systems.summary: Prompts hide only for threats the player can perceive. Live since 10-29 21:22 (Relay v2 step V2, define-free): EXAMINE prompts hide only during a chase and 3 s after it, while a door break's blows are heard within 36 m, or while the Relay is on screen and lit.

systems.name: Warning stages
systems.summary: Walking distance to the Relay sets stages 0 to 2; since 10-22 it drives the W1 lamps and holds the moving wallpaper on plain K00.

systems.name: Stage 1: your lamps
systems.summary: Your room's lamps dip together, never near it (on v1 since 10-22); flickering and failing lamps are held steady (or dim) for the warning and dip with it (M1 + M3, 10-22 20:47). Each burst sags the room-tone hum with them (the ballast groan, since 10-22 15:23).

systems.name: Stage 2: muffled steps
systems.summary: Its steps through walls, muffled by doors, at stage 2 or in sight (+10.3 dB over room tone through a shut door); a faint hum when it stands still (C30). In main since 10-22 15:23.

systems.name: Stage 3: lock-on
systems.summary: A door-holder thunk and one chime when it sees you. The lock-on is built behind the define since 10-30 22:21 (V4b); its sounds are still to do (声音设计).

systems.name: Extra cues
systems.summary: Device sounds, a panel tick, the hum returning, an edge marker.
systems.closed_note: Decided: all; marker off by default (10-21)

systems.name: Chase wave
systems.summary: Lamps ripple out from your room when a chase starts.

systems.name: Wallpaper arrows
systems.summary: The print's arrows turn toward the station TV, then the EXIT (C24 = A + A20), and run with a chase; they never lie (C29) and never glow (A24). Motion: A + M4 + V1 (C31, 10-22). The ambient print motion they sit on is in main since 10-22. Live on desktop since 10-22 21:48, when the route driver landed; phones have turn-only arrows in main since 10-30 23:14 (C34), not yet run on a device, and full arrows wait for a device measure; WebGL shows no cue, and turn-only there is a team call. The station phase is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (wired 17:33, M5); floors below LEVEL 0 wait for M4.
systems.closed_note: Decided: yes (10-07); the exit is set (10-21)

systems.name: Screens join warnings
systems.summary: Parked, not in v1 (C09, Red 10-22): CRTs would show interference at stage 1 and an alarm slate in a chase. Screens never sag or roll with the lamps.

systems.name: Warnings on today's Relay
systems.summary: Both warnings run on today's Relay since 10-22: W1 lamps and W2 steps. The 2D stingers and clicks are gone, tension follows the stage and the drone is gated (C10, C30).

systems.name: Doors: body open, pull shut
systems.summary: Doors open and shut by the body alone since Red's body-door picks (A50; 10-31, switched on 10-31 21:01): no door has a button, USE moves no door; each is a noise heard to about 20 m (v1) or by its verb (V5: ease 6 m, barge 18 m, slam 27 m). As built (Codex, doors only, 10-31 17:14; on in the builds since 10-31 21:01; none of it played yet): a short lean on the latch, then a slow squeeze that rests where you stop (2A), a walking push, or a frontal sprint within 60° (a 0.15 s carry) that bursts it; the only shut is the pull (turn back, rest the dot on the leaf 0.3 s, step back 0.12 s), a SLAM if you sprinted through that door in the last 2.0 s; E shows only a hint (WALK INTO DOOR; STEP BACK TO SHUT for 1.0 s, 11-01 13:57); the unlock ends with the leaf 10° ajar and the body opens it (11B); the start door and the stairwell north door are body doors too (6B); a barge was made smoother on 11-01 21:13 (Red 18:52). Alarm bars (a facing, straight 0.4 s push) are built but inert: alarmDoor = 0. The rulings are A57. Double-acting since 10-22 15:11: the leaf always swings away from whoever moves it, every unlock is a push, and an opened door is never broken. Since 10-30 20:44 every double-acting door has a vision panel, map doors included, one form per zone (A42): within 1.0 m of a shut leaf you peek through it, and the peek runs live (C36, A43), with PEEK on the phone's USE disc since 20:51. The Relay can't see through it, and the wired glass can't be broken; you can see the Relay through it, so a lit door no longer counts as cover in the Relay's unseen tests (map side, 20:54). No map door is a Run door: the low square window belongs to the Run! rooms, which are not on the map yet (M8, 系统设计 10-30).
systems.closed_note: Decided: swing away from the player (10-22)

systems.name: Ease, barge, slam, ajar
systems.summary: Walk into a door to open it softly, sprint into it to barge, turn back and pull to shut or slam; the Relay leaves doors ajar. The Relay's OPEN, which leaves a door ajar at 30°, is built behind the define since 10-30 (V3b); the player's ease, barge and slam were built as V5 (10-31 11:40, behind the define: 6 m +1 / 18 m +8 / 27 m +12, swing lock, the 0.5 m step test) and, since Red's body-door picks (A50), run as contact gaits: a squeeze or walking push is an EASE, a frontal sprint contact within 60° with a 0.15 s carry is a BARGE, and the pull within 2.0 s of sprinting through that door is a SLAM. Source-integrated 10-31 17:14 (Codex, doors only; one ordinary body bot and one controlled chase passed in a clone, no G1 to G8 grade), switched on with the define and bodyDoors = 1 at 10-31 21:01 and shipped in the local 10-31 20:59 builds; the barge was smoothed on 11-01 21:13 (one planned ease-out per swing, the leaf stepped before the body; Red's 18:52 complaint, measured in a clone only). A held door breaks at 0.6 s (3A), a slow try on a locked door is silent (4A), the unlock ends 10° ajar (11B). Since 11-04 a leaf can also be shut by touch, still with no button: PUSH-SHUT (built 06:43: a slow press on the face the leaf hangs toward squeezes it back, a walking press swings it shut and latches it, a sprint into that face slams it) and TOUCH-CLOSE (built 06:57, Red's decision 14, "要，选 B", A63: a press on the face you pushed of a leaf open at rest, 70° or more, with the view facing it, closes it after the walk lean; a quiet EASE, or a SLAM after a run through that door within 2 s). The noise numbers are the same (ease 6 m, slam 27 m). Not yet played by anyone (the combined test and the bot rounds are pending, C44). Rulings: A57. The stamina lever (0.4 s per slam, estimate, off) stays 系统设计's.

systems.name: Broken doors
systems.summary: Broken for the run; E (or USE on phones, since 10-22) is refused, silent (0.55 s guard). The B·4 crosshair and its knock are live with HUD key B since 10-29 (14:49; sounds 15:31). Decided 10-30 (A41): a broken door tears at its top pivot and leans on the bottom one; a half-broken door stays weak, because the Relay resumes from the blows already struck; steel doors take 0.5 s longer; baked debris; a thin light leak shows in the split. Live since 17:40: the look landed at 17:34 (游戏视觉), the map side at 17:40 (关卡设计: kept blows, a steel door takes one blow more). Its sounds landed at 18:00 (声音设计).

systems.name: Glass and climbing
systems.summary: Hold E to break a pane through staged cracks (a loud call, since 10-21); walk into the frame to climb. Cracks are kept between holds and knocks (since 10-22).

systems.name: Quiet sash pry
systems.summary: Hold E on the latch for 4 s: a quiet way through a window. Built as V6 (10-31 00:42, 关卡设计) behind the profile flag sashPry (0 in FrontRoomsLevel0): hold E on the latch for the pry, 8 m and +8, and the Relay's own window step (frame step over the sill, 0 Attention). The latch look landed 10-31 11:37 (游戏视觉, v6_sash_look: box-head pocket double-hungs, KeyHud Pry and PryAlarmed = Hold), the phone's USE disc maps Pry and PryAlarmed to Hold (Mobile.cs, checked 11-01), and 叙事设计 signed the strings on 11-01 13:32 (PRY SASH, SASH OPEN flash; the flash is not built). The flag flips after the combined test (关卡设计). Readings ruled: A55.

systems.name: Alarmed windows
systems.summary: Foil-taped windows that always call the Relay. Built as V7a (10-31 12:44) behind the profile flag foil (0): foil only on chunk-border windows, one foiled window per zone slot from the shared trigger budget; the device trips when the pane or sash gives (45 m, error 0). The look landed 11-01 20:54 (游戏视觉: lead foil on the pane, reed contact on the sash; inert at foil 0) and 叙事设计 signed the ALARMED strings on 11-01 13:32. Readings ruled: A52.

systems.name: Door, lock, key models
systems.summary: Since 10-29 20:23 (D1.6 and map contract v9) every map door except the EXIT wears the D1.6 door, lock and key models, every key is the dressed key (the floor key hangs on the station's hook), and the unlock shot uses it; since 10-30 the leaves are walnut.

systems.name: Locked doors
systems.summary: Locks, rattle, key-turn shot; in play it now locks only Floor 1's EXIT, until the floor key (A13, since 10-29 19:17); inner doors stay unlocked (A13, A35).

systems.name: Keys
systems.summary: Look and E on desktop, USE or a tap on phones (both since 10-22 16:45). Today one per zone, opening nothing; decided 10-22: one floor key per floor, at the station. The floor key is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:58): one 'Key · floor' at the station's key spot, opening the EXIT and any locked door on its floor. In a station run, floors below LEVEL 0 build no zone keys and lock no inner doors (A35, since 17:49).

systems.name: Map, zones, modules
systems.summary: Generated zones, rooms as data, streaming, the Level Designer. Level transitions (frames and renovated crossings) are in main since 10-30 21:37, inert until 关卡设计's map contract lands (A47). Since 11-03 main has four scenes, one job each (A59): the game, the Level Designer, the interactables example (FrontRoomsScreenAdsDemo) and a structures scene where every new structure (pool, dramatic spaces, slides, stairs, modules) is built for Red to walk before it goes into the game.

systems.name: Trigger rooms
systems.summary: Rooms you can read from the doorway; entering sounds an alarm. Built in two steps behind flags: V7a (10-31 12:44) added the one trigger budget per map (FrontRoomsTriggerBudget in FrontRoomsTriggerDevices.cs: one roll per zone, 1/3, 1/2.5, 1/2, 1/1.75, 1/1.5 by the zone's stored tier, one device per slot by kind), and V7b (10-31 13:24) the alarm push-bar door (flag alarmDoor, 0) as its third kind after Run! and foil. The door's look and the crosshair case landed 11-01 20:54 (游戏视觉) and the map contract for Red's 0.4 s bar push 11-01 21:10 (BodyDoors dec70df6); the placard face is a stand-in until 信息设计 delivers. Readings and the Run!-takes-an-alarm-door edge ruled: A53.

systems.name: Sanctuaries
systems.summary: Dead-circuit rooms the Relay will not enter.

systems.name: Relay entries
systems.summary: Where it arrives and leaves; markers live, dead-end entries to build. V7a (10-31, behind foil) adds auto entries: at least 2 per zone, at least 10 cells (Manhattan) apart, at dead ends and corridor ends, recomputed over the built chunks.

systems.name: Map validator
systems.summary: Checks keys can be reached, windows stay passable, cover exists. V7a (10-31) landed the v2 rules in the validator (plain windows per border and zone, entries, device exclusions, cover reported only), V7b the alarm-door rules; both run with their profile flags on.

systems.name: Office dressing
systems.summary: Cubicles, CRTs, piles and wall outlets (in the maze since 10-22); terminal host desks to come.

systems.name: Run! rooms
systems.summary: The alarm corridor: a long trigger room entered through an arch, ending in a door you can shut. Stepping in calls the Relay, and the sprint to the door is the reward. Its look B Emergency Power was decided 10-21 and its kit was built in a clone. Still to come: the trigger room framework, the module, and Red's calls 2 to 8. Run doors and the low square window arrive with it (M8). Dates (schedule R2, re-dated 10-31): an inert kit in main by 11-03; a first playable room only after 关卡设计's map hooks (CR-1 to CR-6, M8), they landed 10-31 01:07, so the inert kit is met; the first playable room is not in the PT4 snapshot (11-03/04), so 11-05 at the earliest (系统设计's uncalibrated target, A54). The trip sounds only the devices' own local sounds, no building bell (C07). The goal door is RN-F with set A's F5 window, never locked; RN-X is retired. Run! is the tier-2 trigger kind, after the run's first send, and keeps the trigger rooms' shared tell at its entrance (系统设计, 10-31). Red decided calls 2 and 5–8 on 10-31 (C38–C43): its own goal door, Office hosts allowed, the title-stream room left alone, no EXIT sign inside, a glowing goal window, and three reference photos. Built-off state 11-01: the map hooks CR-1 to CR-6 and M8 are in main since 10-31 01:07 (master runRooms = 0; runGoalDoorForced = 1 for C38, runInOffice = 1 for C39; a plain-C# planner, one host per chunk, T2+ after the first send, never the arrival zone), 游戏视觉's Run! B corridor is wired to them since 10-31 11:38 and its fixes since 12:41, and Run! shares the one trigger budget with foil and alarm doors (Run! keeps first claim on a Standard zone's slot; foil takes Tall zones'). Frequency is far below one per 2-3 zones (A54: measure first; the table is not raised for Run! alone). The 11-03 inert-kit date is met (it landed 10-31); the playable room waits for the combined test and 总控's word for the runRooms switch-on, and Run! stays off in the PT4 playtest snapshot. Ruled 11-01 (A54): RN-X retired, tier 2 stays, the budget table is not raised for Run! alone, the calm route avoids its armed area (+30 m), and Run! avoids the B-floor station walk (to build). Run! rethink decided 11-03 (A60; design page research/level_space/71_run_room.md; so far only the red tube and its strip are built, 灯具适配 06:33 on 11-04): length by depth (7 cells for the run's first Run!, then 9, 12 from T4, 14 at T5 where it fits, cap 14 cells), one Run! a floor dealt from a per-floor deck that holds "nothing", a plain Run! before any twist, a calm zone beyond the goal door, ramps from T3, an honest Run door entrance from T3 (trip about 2.5 m in, readable from 5 m: A61), the receding end on deep floors only (floor B2 or deeper at T4, B3 or deeper at T5; it trips at the 9 m frame), the model transition, and look B (the alarm pulse, lit by the third, dark oxblood tube in each R-B strip. Red said yes on 11-04: "加，用更亮档", then "用这个点位吧" on the brightest column of 灯具适配's HDR sheet, read as tube linear 3, strip Light 3.5, halo .40; the strip and rig carrying it landed 06:33). The teaching room (the run's first Run! with the pulse off, look A, then B) no longer waits on the tube. The rest is built inert and enters the game only after Red has walked scene 4 (A59).
systems.closed_note: Decided: look B Emergency Power (10-21); gets a date (10-30)

systems.name: Bathroom rooms
systems.summary: Bathroom rooms around a pool (A48). Built so far, inert (11-04 07:14, 总控 with 夸张结构调研与设计, 64 files): the map side of the pool in main's fourth scene, Assets/Scenes/FrontRoomsStructures.unity (not in the build settings), with the pool partials (FrontRoomsMapPool, Plan, Modules, Data, StandIns, Materials, MapWorld.Pool) and hooks that all test Cache.HasPool first, so the game plays as before. Compile-gated only; nothing was run in Unity, and the first Play is Red's. The game has no water yet. Research landed 10-31 00:26 (research/bathroom_rooms/). Its 20_for_red.md asks Red D1–D12, and Red's D picks were in on 10-31 (D1 all) per the bathroom line's cards. Build (schedule R4a, R4b, R4c; the bathroom line's uncalibrated estimate): a playable greybox about 11-07, the v1 look and sound about 11-13, observation windows, court and polish about 11-17, about 284–433 planned hours with water, ray-traced water and the dark zone one level down. Red paused the pool on 11-01 at 17:34 and lifted the pause on 11-03 at 14:19 (A58); the dates moved one day (R4a about 11-08 for a greybox in the structures scene, R4b about 11-14, R4c about 11-18; 系统设计's, uncalibrated) and the pool enters the game only after Red has walked it (A59).

systems.name: Evacuation plan
systems.summary: One printed sheet in the first room by the desk on Floor 1 (A26), with a copy on every stairwell landing; EXAMINE reads it. Red picked sheet A on 10-22: a route diagram that teaches four rules and the locked stair (a Phase 0 variant where the stair is not locked). Since 10-29 19:17 Floor 1's sheet hangs in the first room (the room sheet while the EXIT is locked); floors without a station keep the Phase 0 sheet at the start door (since 10-22 21:03).

systems.name: EXAMINE close-up
systems.summary: E frames the plan or the first key; the game pauses (in main since 10-22); phones open it with USE (READ) and leave with BACK (since 10-22 21:10), a TEXT chip shows the transcript, and zoom works (wheel or right button; pinch or double tap on phones; since 10-24); its sound mix is in since 10-22 12:23 (声音设计's sound_inspect_v2); a focus-loss guard remains. Since 10-30 15:22 only careful reading pauses (A43): the plan, memos and terminal pages pause. Close-ups for looking run live (the first key, one-line signs and the station TV's ad), and a threat or a catch ends them; the door peek has no threat gate (C36). On phones a live close-up has no TEXT chip, no pause button and no back latch, so backing away is one move (since 15:31). A live close-up keeps the live mix (since 18:00). Since 10-30 21:39 a close-up faces its object square on from every side, the station TV keeps its old angle, and one more tap shows the content alone, full bleed (A46).

systems.name: Office terminals
systems.summary: One readable computer per Office zone; E to read its pages. Decided 10-30: the era's own interaction, a DOS text-mode in-house program with CUA keys and a lightbar menu (C19; spec research/computer_ui/41_c19_period_interaction.md); our own 8 × 16 bitmap face (C20; FR816 C20, in main since 14:48); on phones the close-up is full bleed with no TEXT chip or transcript (A39); readable terminals show E·1 (A38). Built in main since 10-30 13:49 (游戏视觉's terminal_a: the 80 × 25 char-grid terminal, MAIN / DOC / LIST / HELP, the READ close-up at 70 % with TEXT on desktop and iPad, 95 % without on phones), inert until a desk calls it (关卡设计's L2; the close-up's input branch landed 10-30 15:22, touch tap and swipe 15:42). The strings are in since 14:57, three more memo sets since 15:24, and the program is named OFFICE MEMO (INTEROFFICE was a real Oracle product).

systems.name: Crosshair states
systems.summary: One grammar for door, lock, broken door and the look-eye, live with HUD key B since 10-29 14:49 (the map's AimKind feed, Read/Examine E·1). The station-TV eye (C35) is live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:41; E · WATCH TV on the playing station TV since 10-30 15:23, WATCH on the phone's USE disc since 15:31, A44). Readable computer terminals show E·1 too, and dark or still desk screens never (A38, 10-30; to build with the terminals).

systems.name: Key and lock HUD motion
systems.summary: HUD key B is live since 10-29 14:49: the key slides in (on the instant pickup the glyph plays P4 alone, KP-1b), and the padlock opens at the crosshair; the unlock shot keeps the panel, C27 (d). Its sounds are live since 15:31 (flight, land, lock tug, unlock drop, broken door).

systems.name: Desk monitors
systems.summary: Ad_03 (WTCZ, since 10-22) plays on the desk monitors of floors without a station; decided 10-22: still screens in the maze, the ad only on the title and station TVs. On Floor 1, since 10-29 19:17, the desk monitors show still screens and the station TV plays the ad with its READ close-up (R3).

systems.name: Exit and win
systems.summary: One EXIT per floor; a stairwell behind it leads one floor deeper (LEVEL 0, then B1, B2, ...); a run ends only when caught; the tier carries over (in main since 10-22 15:39). The stairwell safe zone is in main since 16:05 (A27): no sight, catch or hearing inside, a chase ends at its door, and the Relay stops there, then walks off; since 17:06 its sound agrees (no hum or groan inside, tension at its floor). The lock and the floor key (A13) are live on Floor 1 since 10-29 19:17 (in main since 16:58): the EXIT is locked from the floor's start and opens with the floor key and the unlock shot. In a station run, floors below LEVEL 0 keep an unlocked EXIT until they get their own stations (A35).
systems.closed_note: Decided: an EXIT per floor leads deeper (10-21)

systems.name: Exit signs
systems.summary: Lit, dim and loose EXIT signs; the LIT-locked one over each floor's EXIT is in main since 10-22 15:39 (C23 step 1); chevron signs in its zone later. systems.summary: Floor 1 teaches the loop. Since 16:58 the EXIT is locked from the floor's start and the floor key opens it with the unlock shot (M3), and taking the key kills the TV and turns the arrows to the EXIT; a Relay already out is called to the station (A14). The third-zone fallback is dropped (A40). Bots on 10-30 (v1): an arrow-follower is at the EXIT 16.6 s after Space, so its first encounter is on B1; wanderers reach 150 cells in 125–154 s. Every first chase in those runs was a catch (8 of 8), but only the two evader06 runs try to flee, and both started inside 6 m. Today's sight usually first sees the player at a corner about 6 m away. On B1 (14:44, 2 seeds) evader06 escaped 1 of 2: the escape started at 12 m. Since 15:15 (V3c) the first send's lamps come on as it arrives (C32). C37 (10-30) keeps the 0.7 m catch and adds a longer hold on a close first sighting, behind the define.

EGRESS fits: a fire stair leads to the next floor of the same building. It gives the arrows (C08), the EXIT signs (C23) and the route (C24) a target. Rough cost: 关卡设计 2 to 3 days for the map and game minimum (a map-built stairwell room: the exit door shuts and locks behind you like the start door, the old map is released, a new seed starts at the stairwell's far door, the tier carries over, a FLOOR count on CAUGHT, a placement rule reachable without glass). Not included: the EXIT sign in the map and the stairwell look (游戏视觉), the arrows (C08, +1 to 2 days), strings and type. An escape that ends the run costs about the same plus an ending, and breaks the 10-02 rule. No exit costs nothing, but the goal problem stays and C08, C23, C24, N4 and N5 point at nothing.

Sent at 22–30 m after 1 s, stage 1 starts on arrival and the first burst falls 1.3–2 s after the take. That is honest, because it really is near; the Floor 1 grace still bars a chase before a burst. It breaks v2's 42 m Arrive rule for this one send only. Alternatives: a station farther past the EXIT does not help (the gap never closes while the player walks); keeping 42 m and extending the grace to Floor 2 teaches W1 by the placard only; a scripted burst on the take would make the lamps lie.
decisions.answer: 1: Floor 1's first send only, 1 s after the take, unseen, at 22–30 m, on the station's far side from the EXIT and never within 2 cells of the walk back (fallback 18–34 m, then ≥ 14 cells, logged); the station keeps ≥ 2 Steady lamps by its entrance (retimed by A26 on 10-22: on Floor 1 the first send now comes when you leave the first room, 2 cells out of the room with the key taken (the start door's shut does not count), from the far side, with the 150 s fallback; the rest holds) (amended 10-30 by A40: the gentle arrival now belongs to the run's first send wherever it happens, on Floor 1 after the onboarding threshold or on B1 if the player leaves first; it no longer follows the key take, and its step-in uses the tier's arrive delay, 3 s at T1, ruled by 系统设计 for 关卡设计; its placement is anchored on the player and the FLOW target; landed 10-30 12:41) (10-30 15:15, V3c, live on every path: rungs 1 and 2 also need W ≤ 30 m at the cell, so the lamps warn as it arrives; on seed 20388 the first warning went from 51.3 s after the send to 0.02 s)

decisions.question: Catch distance: keep 0.7 m or go to about 1.3 m, and does a close first sighting get an extra beat?

Of the 5 with an evading bot: 1 was caught before it could react (4.1 m), 3 were caught running (5.7, 5.8 and 4.6 m, the last after 10 s), and 1 escaped (12 m, B1). None of these runs had V4b, so there was no spotting meter, gate, 0.7 s hold or ramp. Worked estimate, not simulated: a player 3 m away at lock-on has 1.52 s after the cue to start running with a 0.7 m catch and 1.39 s with 1.3 m, against 0.55 s in today's game. So V4b adds about 1 s and 1.3 m takes away about 0.15 s. Options: 1 keep 0.7 m and finish V4b; 2 go to 1.3 m now (游戏视觉's HR16: it reads as a reach, but Hunter B is not in main, so that gain cannot be seen yet); 3 option 1 plus about 1 s more on a first sighting inside 6 m (a small V4b change; it gives more time closer in, 3.2 s at 5.9 m against 2.2 s at 6.1 m). It blocks nothing today: V4a and V4b build with 0.7 m, and the answer is needed before V4b's test round. The formal G5 grade comes after V5, because G5 allows eased doors. Asked by 系统设计 in its own chat on 2026-10-30.
decisions.answer: 3: the catch stays 0.7 m, V4b is built as designed, and on the first lock-on of an encounter, within 6 m of the player, the Relay holds 1.7 s instead of 0.7 s before it chases. 系统设计 read "first" as the first lock-on of each encounter; re-acquisitions keep 0.35 s. It is fixed at every tier, touch lock-ons count, and 6 m and the extra 1 s are starting points for playtest. In a paired test, no extra hold gave 15 % and a 9 m radius 50 %, against 40 % as built (+2 escapes, none lost). T1 53 %, T5 36 %, near G5's bars. Whether to widen 6 m to 9 m was asked of Red on 10-31; 6 m stays until then. **Widened to 9 m** on 10-31 (Red in the 系统设计 chat, 10-31 00:32: "全部按推荐", answering the radius question with the indicative round): a first lock-on within 9 m holds 1.7 s

decisions.answer: Ruled by 系统设计 on 2026-11-01 (a ruling on this line's own numbers and wording, not Red's word; Red's picks are A50). RELAY section 10 now reads so. (1) VERBS ARE CONTACT GAITS. The number rows are V5's and do not change: EASE 0.55 s / 6 m / +1, BARGE 0.3 s / 18 m / +8, SLAM 0.3 s / 27 m / +12, rattle 6 m / +1. A squeeze (slow gait) and a walking push are EASE; a frontal sprint contact within 60° is BARGE, and letting go of RUN up to 0.15 s before contact still counts; the pull is an EASE, or a SLAM when the player's feet crossed that door's line sprinting within the last 2.0 s and the step back is at walk speed or more (a slow step back after a run is the quiet shut). The two windows are different things: 2.0 s is a crossing record by door edge for the pull, 0.15 s is a release carry for the barge. One DoorMoved per verb and one verb per contact episode per door (it ends 0.5 s or 0.5 m after the body leaves), so inching never doubles a noise. The unlock's noise moves to the first body push (6 m / +1, or a barge): the key turn leaves the leaf 10° ajar and raises no DoorMoved (11B). (2) REPLACED, FOR THE PLAYER ONLY: 'E to open or shut' and the fast test (sprinting, or up to 0.5 s after a sprint frame). The bots keep TryOpenDoor, PlayerFast and the 0.5 s, so G5 and every baseline stay comparable; they measure nothing about body doors until the -autopilotBodyDoors round. (3) FREE, NO NOISE AND NO ATTENTION: the lean on the latch (design values 0.12 s walk, 0.30 s slow, 0.40 s blind push, 交互设计's estimates), a slow try on a locked door (4A), a broken door's wobble, a bump while the key is in hand, a blocked thud; a leaf at rest at 70° or more is a wall. (4) AJAR WIDENS: a leaf between 3° and 70° is Ajar (+4 m, blocks sight, the Relay pushes through in 0.4 s), whether the Relay's 30°, a crack the player left (2A) or the unlock's 10° (11B). RELAY's old line 'Ajar stays 30°; 10° would be hard to read' now holds for the Relay's own Ajar only. Ajar no longer means only 'the Relay came through'; the playtest checks that a player can still read a trace from a door. A pull shuts and latches any Ajar leaf whole (+9 m, a WALL to a Relay without a licence). (5) HELD DOOR (3A): a Relay OPEN or PUSH whose leaf has rested on the player for 0.6 s becomes a BREAK at once with no licence, and a break throw stopped by the player's body outside a sanctuary is a catch; holding a door buys about 0.6 s plus one break (1.9 to 2.5 s), then it is over. The design says the catch also reaches v1; 系统设计 did not read the code. (6) THE CHASE PRICE is in time, turns and doors, not Attention (frozen while the Relay is on the map): from the stop to the latch about 0.9 s on a mouse, 1.6 to 2.0 s on touch, 1.9 to 2.5 s on a pad (交互设计's estimates, uncalibrated, and the turn rates are caps, not measurements); a Relay at 4.2 to 4.4 m/s closes about 4 m, 7 to 9 m, 8 to 11 m in that time; a slam that lands buys one break (2.5 s at tier 1, 1.9 s at the top). So a chase slam favours fast turners; Red accepted this with 1C and the same rule runs on every device. The stamina lever (0.4 s per slam, ESTIMATE, 0 by default) stays 系统设计's: if more price is wanted it is the lever, never Attention. (7) SPECIAL DOORS. The start door and the stairwell north door are body doors (6B) and raise no Relay noise (the start door opens before any Relay exists, the north door opens out of the safe stairwell); their shut-behind stays scripted, and the start door stays latched, with a strain cue, while the map streams. An alarm bar (10A) opens only to a facing (60°), straight (30°) push held 0.4 s; a barge or a graze is a hard stop with ALARMED; the trip stays the map's one open (A53). The EXIT seal stays the only door that shuts itself besides those two. (8) G5: 'shut the door and walk away' now costs a stop, a turn and 0.12 s of step; the evader bot still shuts through TryOpenDoor, so G5's grade is unchanged and says nothing about a human at a mouse, a pad or a thumb; 关卡设计调研's chase bot measures that after the combined test (not a Red item). (9) BUILT AND LIVE, as the landings say. Source-integrated by Codex on 10-31 17:14 (56 paths, dark; acceptance 17:20 in a silenced clone: core 41/0, special 21/0, shots 257/0, ordinary body bot 15 opens in 198 cells, one controlled chase with 5 barges and 5 pull slams, a three-floor key, EXIT and north-door traversal). glossary.definition: The director’s noise meter for one run. Player noises add to it: sprint step +3, barge +8, slam +12, pry +8, ease a door or unlock +1, walking 0. It drains 3 per second (2 at tier 5), starting 3 s after the last noise. At the threshold (60 at tier 1, down to 45 at tier 5) the Relay is called to the area of the noise, never to the exact spot.

How much threat the player has perceived in the current encounter. Only perceived cues count: lamps +1/s, steps +2.5/s, seeing the Relay +4/s, the chase +6/s, a lock-on +15. At the peak the director holds for 4 s (SUSTAIN), then fades the encounter and the Relay withdraws.
A difficulty step. Today it rises with zones visited plus a stall rule; v2 proposes one tier per 150 newly explored cells. Tiers make the Relay better, never the warnings shorter.

The Relay may lock on only after the warning has run continuously for at least 3 s (stage 1 or higher), including at least 1 s of continuous stage 2 (steps). The timers reset when the stage drops. Only a lock-on at touching distance (1.5 m) is exempt.

The Relay’s distance to the player along real walking paths (a shut door adds 9 m), never more than three times the straight line. It sets the warning stages: stage 1 at 30 m or less, stage 2 at 18 m or less.
The guaranteed calm after the Relay leaves: 100 s at tier 1, 60 s at tier 5. Noise cannot call it back during RELAX; glass and alarm devices still can.

The Relay may break a door only if a sound it heard came through that door, or it saw the player cross it or heard it move. It may quietly open the doors that were shut on its route when it was sent. Any other shut door is a wall to it.
When a quiet player goes 240 s (tier 1) without a call, the director sends the Relay to patrol a zone ahead of them, aimed at the area, never the exact spot.
The warning level in the player’s own room: 0 nothing, 1 lamps dip, 2 muffled steps, 3 the lock-on chime.
The director sending the Relay toward an area, because Attention crossed its threshold, a device was tripped, or a sweep is due.
